what_its_for: Cetirizine is an antihistamine used to relieve allergy symptoms such as runny nose, sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and itchy skin. It is also used to treat hives (urticaria) and skin itching caused by allergies. It works by blocking histamine, a natural substance your body makes during an allergic reaction.
how_to_take: Take cetirizine exactly as directed on the label or as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid form, measure your dose carefully using the measuring cup or spoon that comes with the medicine — do not use a regular kitchen spoon. Chewable tablets should be chewed completely before swallowing.
dosing: Adults and children 6 years and older: The usual dose is 5 mg to 10 mg once daily. Do not take more than 10 mg in one day. Children 2 to 5 years old: The usual dose is 2.5 mg once daily, or up to 5 mg once daily or in two divided doses of 2.5 mg. Children under 2 years: Do not use unless directed by a doctor. If you have kidney or liver problems, your doctor may recommend a lower dose. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions for your situation.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store cetirizine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking cetirizine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Be careful when driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing any activity that requires you to be alert, especially when you first start taking this medicine. Avoid taking other antihistamines, sleep aids, or anxiety medications at the same time without asking your doctor or pharmacist first, as these can increase side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: a severe allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness; extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up; fast or uneven heartbeat; difficulty urinating; or if your symptoms do not improve after a few days or get worse. Also tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or have kidney or liver problems before taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Cetirizine starts working within 1 hour of taking it. You should notice relief from your allergy symptoms fairly quickly. For best results with ongoing allergies, take it at the same time each day. It provides up to 24 hours of relief from a single dose.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): Use with caution as drowsiness and dizziness may increase your risk of falling. A lower dose of 5 mg per day is often recommended. Kidney or liver disease: A lower dose is usually recommended — talk to your doctor before use. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking cetirizine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of cetirizine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before using if you are breastfeeding. Children under 2 years: Do not use without a doctor's guidance.
